intended_object: The canonical isomorphism K₀(∏ᵢ Rᵢ) ≅ ∏ᵢ K₀(Rᵢ) for a finite family of rings. Its components are the maps induced by the coordinate projections Rᵢ → Rᵢ, i.e. by scalar extension along each projection. This comes from the docstring and from the use of `piMap`.
explanation:
The definition is `AddEquiv.ofBijective` applied to `piMap Ri`. `piMap` is the map whose i-th component is `K0.map (Pi.evalRingHom Ri i)`, the map induced on K₀ by scalar extension along the i-th projection ∏ R → Rᵢ. So the underlying map is the canonical comparison map, as it should be.

The bijectivity proof works at the level of monoids. It goes through the equivalence of monoids of finitely generated projective classes, `ProjectiveClass.piEquiv`, and uses the fact that group completion (localization at the top submonoid) commutes with products. Since the definition compiles, the proof is valid.

The `Finite ι` hypothesis is the standard setting and is needed. For an infinite product, finitely generated projective modules over ∏ Rᵢ do not decompose into families of uniformly bounded rank, so the map is not surjective in general. Arbitrary rings, not necessarily commutative, are allowed. That is the natural generality.

Mathlib has no algebraic K₀ of rings and no such isomorphism, so there is no counterpart to cite.
